els.text: Forty seats around one fire. A short menu that changes with what the farms send, bread from the oven every hour, and wine from people we know.
Prices in pounds. Tell us about allergies when you book.

els.text: The oven is lit at two and runs at 450 degrees by five. Everything on the menu passes through it at least once, even the pudding.

els.alt: The dining room at night, lamps on every table

els.text: A long room on the ground floor of an old cotton warehouse. Sit at the counter to watch the fire, or at the long table, which seats fourteen and can be yours for the evening.

els.text: Natural and low-intervention wine from small growers, most of it by the glass. Beer from three breweries within a mile. Proper tea, and a hot chocolate made with the same honey as the tart.
Ask for the list at the table.

els.alt: A table laid for dinner under a small lamp

els.text: A fire, a room, and ten people who like cooking on it.

els.alt: Nell Ashby at the pass, slicing carrots

els.text: Cinder opened in 2019 on the ground floor of an old cotton warehouse. Nell had run kitchens in London for twelve years and wanted three things: one fire, one room, and a menu short enough to change every day.
Most of what we cook comes from within a day’s drive. When the boats do not go out, there is no fish, and the menu says so.

els.text: Kitchen closes an hour before we do.
New Islington stop, then five minutes along the canal.
Ten minutes from Piccadilly station, up Great Ancoats Street.
One level from the street door to the table, and a step-free loo.

els.alt: The wood oven, lit, with bread on the hearth

els.text: It sits beside the oven, so you watch your dinner cooked. A set menu from £55 a head, and the room is yours from seven until we close.

sections.heading: Book a table
sections.text: Tell us the day, the time and how many of you. We confirm by email, usually within the hour. For tonight, ring 0161 496 0000.
